slides.title: What a business does
slides.slide: L1 Basic · What a business does
slides.notes: Name what a business makes or sells, who buys it and what it needs to start. Notes: pick a local bakery; learners list its inputs, its customers and one risk, using no formal terms yet.

slides.title: Ownership and aims
slides.notes: Explain sole trader, partnership and company forms and the idea of limited liability. Notes: an owner invests 10,000 and the business fails owing 40,000; a sole trader may owe the rest personally, a company shareholder loses at most 10,000.

slides.title: Marketing mix and break-even
slides.slide: L3 Foundation · Marketing mix and break-even
slides.notes: Apply product, price, place and promotion to a case and calculate break-even. Notes: fixed costs 6,000, price 20 and variable cost 8 give contribution 12 per unit, so break-even is 500 units; learners test a price of 22.

slides.title: People and labour turnover
slides.slide: L4 Practitioner · People and labour turnover
slides.notes: Compare leadership styles and calculate labour turnover with a view on cause. Notes: 6 leavers from an average of 120 staff is 5 per cent; learners suggest two causes, one pay related and one not, and say what evidence would separate them.

slides.title: Investment appraisal
slides.notes: Calculate payback and average return and recommend whether to invest. Notes: an outlay of 50,000 with cash inflows of 20,000 a year pays back in 2.5 years; learners say what the method ignores, such as cash after year 3.

slides.title: Discounted cash flow and strategy
slides.slide: L6 Advanced · Discounted cash flow and strategy
slides.notes: Evaluate a project using net present value and link it to strategic fit. Notes: an outlay of 100,000 and inflows of 40,000 for three years at 10 per cent give a present value of about 99,474, so NPV is about minus 526; test sensitivity to the rate.

slides.title: Cost of capital and governance
slides.slide: L7 Super expert · Cost of capital and governance
slides.notes: Create a recommendation on a merger using weighted cost of capital, synergy and board oversight. Notes: 60 per cent equity at 10 per cent and 40 per cent debt at 5 per cent after tax gives 8 per cent; accept only if risk-adjusted synergies beat it.
